newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-WALKER LEDS U.S. IN PAN PACIFIC HEATS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WALKER LEDS U.S. IN PAN PACIFIC HEATS.

text.p: Neil Walker and Jenny Thompson of the United States both swam career bests to led qualifiers on Tuesday at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships.
Overall, Americans qualified first in four of the six preliminary events and are also favoured in the two freestyle relays to be run on Tuesday evening.

Thompson's personal best of 59.17 made her the fastest qualifier in the women's 100 butterfly final ahead of teammate Misty Hyman (59.92). Japan's Ayari Aoyama, who uses a submarine start like Hyman, was third.
Thompson, a five-time Olympic champion, won gold in the 100 freestyle and anchored the U.S. team to victory in the 4x200 freestyle relay on Monday.

Walker's 53.04 in the 100 butterfly heats made him the fastest qualifier ahead of Michael Klim (53.12) of Australia, who has already won golds in Fukuoka in the 100 and 200 freestyle races, and fellow American Nathaniel Dusing.

American Brooke Bennett topped the heats in the women's 400 freestyle in 4:10.68, but could have trouble holding off Costa Rica's Claudia Poll (4:13.06), who swam the third-fastest time ever to win the 200 freestyle on Sunday.
Australian Grant Hackett, 17, was first in the men's 400 freestyle heats, ahead of Americans Chad Carvin and John Piersma.
Lenny Krayzelburg was the fourth American to qualify first, coming in ahead of teammate Brad Bridgewater and Canadian Mark Versfeld in the men's 200 backstroke preliminaries.

Mai Nakamura, who gave the host country its only gold of the meeting so far with a win in the women's 100 backstroke on Sunday, finished ahead of American Lea Loveless to top the 200 backstroke heats.
The finals of the men's and women's 4x100 freestyle relays will also be contested on Tuesday night, with the United States heavily favoured in both races.
About 300 swimmers from 22 countries and regions are competing in the Pan Pacific Championships.
